environment: Node 22.14 and PostgreSQL 17.11 using private local fixtures
observations: The checkpoint rejected registration before sealing. Two concurrent attempts to register the exact same successor returned the identical signed link.
A competing successor was refused without creating its origin. The checkpoint runtime role could not read the link table and the immutable trigger rejected updates.
Each separately seeded source fixture admitted and completed a synthetic account deletion. The independent owner sealed both archive segments with their own writer and authority keys.
The real offline verifier accepted the ordered linked window and rejected a missing final archive, reordered inputs, a changed link signature and a substituted public key.
The operator exported the exact old bytes and successor link using public keys after both source clusters were removed.
scope: The second fixture was seeded separately at the successor binding. This is archive-link verification and does not establish an in-place source switch or multi-segment restore application.
The provider was simulated. Independent PostgreSQL registration, archive sealing, source checks and operator CLI were exercised.
The optional billing PostgreSQL unit skip is exercised in the wire suite. Hosted services were not modified.
